title: Foreign branch income — s 23AH ITAA 1936
summary: Facet map: is foreign branch income of a resident company exempt under s 23AH? Spine: resident company (not trustee — s 23AH(15)) → foreign PE in listed/unlisted country (s 23AH(2)) / capital gains on PE assets (s 23AH(3)-(4), not TAP) → ships/aircraft carve-out (s 23AH(14A)-(14B)) → hybrid mismatch (s 23AH(4A), (14C)-(14D)) → active income test (s 23AH(12)) → tainted exceptions (s 23AH(5) listed EDCI, (7) unlisted adjusted tainted income, (6)/(8) tainted assets) → disposal/interposition (s 23AH(9)-(11)). FACETS: AIT machinery and s 23AH(14) PE-company/HQ-company assumptions, adjusted tainted income and tainted assets (s 23AH(13)/(15)), listed vs unlisted countries (ss 320-321), hybrid mismatch detail (Div 832), definitions (s 23AH(15)). Subsection coverage: all of s 23AH(1)-(15) mapped. Rulings: TR 2014/3, TR 2002/5.

nodes.label: An Australian resident company derives foreign income (or a capital gain/loss) through a foreign branch — is it exempt under s 23AH?
nodes.body: Single question with facets. Spine: resident company → foreign PE → ships/hybrid carve-outs → active income test → tainted exceptions. Facets carry the machinery and definitions.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Is the taxpayer a resident company (not a trustee)?
nodes.body: s 23AH(15): 'company' does not include a company in the capacity of a trustee. The exemption is only for resident companies.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Not a resident company — s 23AH does not apply
nodes.body: Individuals, trusts and non-residents use the FITO rules (Div 770 ITAA 1997) instead.

nodes.label: Is the income derived in carrying on a business at or through a PE in a listed or unlisted country?
nodes.body: s 23AH(2): foreign income through a PE in a listed/unlisted country is NANE. s 23AH(3)-(4): capital gains/losses on assets used wholly/mainly for foreign income through the PE are disregarded (unless taxable Australian property — s 23AH(3)(c)). s 23AH(9): income from disposing of the business itself is covered.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: No foreign PE — s 23AH does not apply
nodes.body: Foreign income is assessable with FITO relief (Div 770 ITAA 1997). TR 2014/3, TR 2002/5 explain PE.

rulings.title: carrying on a business at or through a permanent establishment
a place at or through which a person carries on any business

nodes.label: Is the income from operating ships or aircraft in international traffic?
nodes.body: s 23AH(14A): the section does NOT apply to ships/aircraft international traffic income (or ancillary things). s 23AH(14B): operates a ship/aircraft in international traffic = transporting passengers/goods between places in different countries.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: International shipping/aircraft — outside s 23AH
nodes.body: Excluded (s 23AH(14A)). Often exempt under the DTA shipping article or subject to FITO.

nodes.label: Is there a branch hybrid mismatch (Div 832 ITAA 1997)?
nodes.body: s 23AH(4A): the exemption does not apply to branch hybrid mismatch income. s 23AH(14C): an amount is branch hybrid mismatch income to the extent it would give rise to a branch hybrid mismatch under Div 832. s 23AH(14D): PE in Div 832 takes the s 23AH meaning.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Branch hybrid mismatch income — not exempt
nodes.body: Assessable despite the PE (s 23AH(4A)).

nodes.label: Does the PE pass the active income test (s 23AH(12))?
nodes.body: Mirrors the CFC test in s 432, modified by s 23AH(12): apply the s 23AH(14) assumptions and ignore ss 432(3), 446(2), 432(1)(b), (e), 447(1)(b), (d), (f). A PE passes if adjusted tainted income (s 23AH(13)) is less than 5% of gross income.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: PE passes the AIT — exemption applies
nodes.body: Foreign income is NANE (s 23AH(2)); capital gains/losses on non-tainted assets disregarded (ss 23AH(3)-(4)).

nodes.label: PE fails the AIT — is the income adjusted tainted income (or EDCI for listed)?
nodes.body: s 23AH(5) listed: AIT failure + adjusted tainted income + eligible designated concession income → no exemption. s 23AH(7) unlisted: AIT failure + adjusted tainted income → no exemption. s 23AH(6)/(8): tainted assets remove the capital gain/loss disregard.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Not adjusted tainted income — exemption applies despite AIT failure
nodes.body: AIT failure only bites on tainted amounts; other income remains NANE.

nodes.label: Income/gain assessable (exemption denied)
nodes.body: s 23AH(5)/(7) deny the income exemption; s 23AH(6)/(8) deny the gain disregard. FITO may apply (Div 770).

nodes.label: Interposed partnerships/trusts and business disposal are also covered (ss 23AH(9)-(11))
nodes.body: s 23AH(9): disposal income treated as business income. s 23AH(10)-(11): indirect interests through partnerships/trusts treated as derived through the company's own PE.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: s 23AH analysis complete
nodes.body: Foreign branch income is NANE unless: hybrid mismatch (4A), ships/aircraft (14A), AIT failure + tainted amounts (5)/(7), tainted assets (6)/(8), or taxable Australian property (3)(c).

nodes.label: FACET — AIT machinery: the s 23AH(14) assumptions
nodes.body: Where to look: s 23AH(12)-(14). The AIT is computed on assumptions isolating the PE: (a) only PE income counted (except for the 447(1)(a)/(c)/(e) and 450(6)(c)/(7)(d)/(8)(b) tainted-income paragraphs); (b) statutory accounting periods = years of income; (c) the PE is treated as a separate 'PE company' dealing wholly independently with the 'HQ company', with HQ income disregarded; (d) AFI entity assumptions; (e) HQ company treated as an associate of the PE company for 447(1)(a)/(c)/(e).

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: FACET — Adjusted tainted income and tainted assets
nodes.body: Where to look: s 23AH(13) (adjusted tainted income = Part X adjusted tainted income on the s 23AH(14) assumptions, ignoring s 446(2) and 447(1)(b),(d),(f)); s 23AH(15) definitions (tainted asset, eligible designated concession income). Passive income — interest, royalties, certain dividends, rents — is typically tainted. The EDCI overlay (s 23AH(5)(c)(ii)) only bites for listed countries.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: FACET — Listed vs unlisted countries (s 320-321 Part X)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 320 (listed countries — comprehensive DTA + suitable tax system), s 321 (unlisted countries), Part X generally. The distinction drives which tainted-income exception applies (EDCI overlay for listed; adjusted tainted income for both). A country's status changes — check the current regulations.

nodes.label: FACET — Branch hybrid mismatch (Div 832 ITAA 1997)
nodes.body: Where to look: Div 832 ITAA 1997 (hybrid mismatch rules — BEAP), s 832-575 (branch hybrid mismatch income), s 23AH(14C)-(14D). The s 23AH(4A) carve-out applies where a payment received by the company would otherwise give rise to a branch hybrid mismatch — the exemption is denied to the extent of the mismatch.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: FACET — Definitions (s 23AH(15))
nodes.body: Where to look: s 23AH(15). 'company' excludes trustee companies; 'double tax agreement' has the Part X meaning; 'foreign income' includes amounts that would otherwise be assessable under non-CGT provisions; 'PE' is the Part X/DTA meaning; 'tainted asset' and 'eligible designated concession income' adopt the Part X definitions.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

edges.label: No — no PE in a listed/unlisted country
Yes — adjusted tainted income / tainted asset + EDCI
